title: `select` refuses before `fetch` has run (R1005 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of `docs/plans/oracle/refuse-on-missing-artifact.md` — **OD-9 / R1005**.

`select` with an index but no `data/transcripts/` directory now exits 1 naming `fetch`, instead of printing a threshold report in which no video could possibly have passed the threshold. That is the same understatement BL-7 found one stage over: it reads as a measurement of the lever and is really one of the missing corpus.

**`select_all`'s docstring is corrected rather than extended**, because getting this sentence wrong is how the tolerance gets restored by accident. A missing transcript **for a video** is not an error — a title hit needs no caption track (R2, R24). A missing **cache directory** is.

**An empty cache directory selects normally** — title hits in, everything else out at zero canonicals. That is the test which separates R1005's two sentences, and it is the reason the check is on the directory rather than on its contents.

The cache is checked **after** the alias table, so a stage missing both still names the table and the existing refusal keeps its wording and position.

`_missing` now takes the error rather than its filename: a `MissingArtifact` already carries all three parts of the sentence. The alias table keeps its own wording, deliberately — no stage produces it (R1007 calls it hand-authored input), so R1005's "name the stage that produces it" has no answer for it.

**Four existing tests gain a `fetched(config)` call.** The helper exists so the reason is written once: tests about "fetch ran and cached nothing for this video" must now create the directory that says fetch ran. Before R1005 those were one state on disk, so no test had to say which it meant.

9 new tests, 541 passing.

Carries a merge of the base branch so the required checks run against the tree this will land on.
